Column mapping for tabular TOC sources

Source: R/toc.R
toc_schema.Rd

Describes how a TOC stored as a flat table (a database table, CSV or RDS file, or data frame) maps onto the canonical TOC fields. Column names are matched case-insensitively. Multi-line cells are split on delim.

Usage

toc_schema(
  program = "program_name",
  type = "output_type",
  number = "output_number",
  title = "output_title",
  subtitle = "output_subtitle",
  footnotes = "output_footnotes",
  output_file_name = "output_file_name",
  scope = c("study", "milestone"),
  delim = "\\"
)

Arguments

program

Column(s) holding the program name. When several are given, the first non-blank value in each row wins.

type, number, title, subtitle, footnotes, output_file_name

Columns holding each field. Use NA for a field the source does not have.

scope

Columns that scope a row, for example to a study or milestone. A named vector renames them: c(study = "study_id") exposes column study_id as scope key study.

delim

Line delimiter inside multi-line cells.

Value

An object of class toc_schema.

Examples

toc_schema(program = c("r_program", "program_name"), scope = c(study = "study_id"))
#> $program
#> [1] "r_program"    "program_name"
#> 
#> $type
#> [1] "output_type"
#> 
#> $number
#> [1] "output_number"
#> 
#> $title
#> [1] "output_title"
#> 
#> $subtitle
#> [1] "output_subtitle"
#> 
#> $footnotes
#> [1] "output_footnotes"
#> 
#> $output_file_name
#> [1] "output_file_name"
#> 
#> $scope
#>      study 
#> "study_id" 
#> 
#> $delim
#> [1] "\\"
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "toc_schema"
